title: Magnolia Three-Day Weather/Sky Report: Orionid meteor shower approaches peak
excerpt: South Arkansas enters the new workweek as October's Orionid meteor shower approaches its annual peak.
content:
South Arkansas enters the new workweek as October's Orionid meteor shower approaches its annual peak.

Daytime highs will be near 80. Overnight lows will be near 45.

All times in this report are Central Daylight.

THREE-DAY FORECAST

Monday, October 19: Brilliant sunshine, high near 80 degrees, low around 44. East-southeast wind near 6 mph.

Tuesday, October 20: Sunny, high near 81, low around 44. East-northeast wind near 6 mph.

Wednesday, October 21: Sunny, high near 82, low around 45. Northeast wind near 5 mph.

SUNRISE AND SUNSET

Date                       Sunrise                Sunset

Monday                   7:19 a.m.            6:36 p.m.

Tuesday                  7:20 a.m.             6:35 p.m.

Wednesday             7:21 a.m.             6:34 p.m.

MOONRISE AND MOONSET

Day                        Moonrise              Moonset

Monday                  3:02 p.m.             12:39 a.m.

Tuesday                 3:33 p.m.              1:39 a.m.

Wednesday             4:01 p.m.             2:38 a.m.

TROPICAL WEATHER

The National Hurricane Center reported early Monday that no tropical cyclones were active in the Atlantic basin, including the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico.

EARTHQUAKES

The USGS reported no magnitude-2.5-and-greater earthquakes for the preceding 24 hours in Arkansas or surrounding states.

FIREBALLS

The American Meteor Society's publicly accessible records did not establish any verified fireball sightings within 500 miles of Magnolia during the preceding 24 hours.

INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION

There will be no bright passes of the International Space Station over Magnolia in the next three days.

SPACE WEATHER

NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center forecasts possible G1 minor geomagnetic storm conditions Monday and Tuesday because of high-speed solar wind from a coronal hole.

MAGNOLIA OBSERVATORY

The Orionid meteor shower, produced by debris from Halley's Comet, peaks overnight Wednesday into Thursday. NASA estimates 10-20 meteors hourly under ideal dark skies. A bright waxing gibbous Moon will interfere with observations, making the hours after moonset and before dawn preferable.

U.S. SPACECRAFT LAUNCHES

Bandwagon-5: Cape Canaveral, Florida, Monday, October 19, with a scheduled window of 5:30-6:30 a.m. This rideshare mission carries multiple spacecraft.

Starlink: Vandenberg Space Force Base, California, Tuesday, October 20, with a scheduled window of 5:14-9:14 p.m.
